payload.headline: Tesla slips 2.43% to 374.41 below key averages; margins and cash still shrinking, avoid

summary.thesis: Tesla's sales have stalled and its margins and cash flow are shrinking, yet the stock is priced at 14.3 times sales, near the top of its own 5-year range.
summary.decision: Long-term: avoid. Swing: no trade before the 2027-01-27 report.
summary.act_at: Re-examine near 293.94 only if operating margin rises back above 3.35%

payload.happening: The stock fell 2.43% to 374.41, down from 383.72. It closed below its 20-day average (386.12), its 200-day average (381.92) and its 50-day average (376.03), and the trend is down. There is no news since the last note. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Today's drop changes sentiment, not the business. What did change the business came in the 2026-10-22 filing. Sales growth stopped: the latest quarter's revenue was -0.17% versus a year earlier, down from 15.78% two quarters ago, and -0.67% versus the prior quarter. Margins are thinner. Operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and gross margin is 19.29%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) fell to 3.3B from 6.8B over twelve months. The filings flag inventory up 15% while quarterly sales grew 0%. Unsold cars can force price cuts, which puts margins at further risk. Investment returns have weakened: each dollar invested now earns 5¢ a year, versus 33¢ three years ago. The balance sheet is not at risk. Tesla has 17.9B in cash against 8.0B of debt, 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity. Dilution is small at 0.43% a year. DATA contains no governance items.

worth.text: At 374.41 the market values Tesla at 1480.0B. That is 14.3 times sales and 412.0 times trailing earnings. The two valuation methods are far apart. A discounted cash flow (DCF) model values the business on the cash it produces, using a 10.1% discount rate. It gives 19.91 (bear), 24.48 (base) and 43.8 (bull). Even 30% starting growth only lifts the DCF to 44.29. If operating margin slips to 1%, it drops to 21.41. The second method assumes the market keeps paying Tesla's usual price-to-sales multiple. It gives 203.8 (low), 293.94 (mid) and 399.81 (high). The price sits between the mid and the high, at the 75th percentile of the stock's own 5-year price-to-sales history. The filings note that the price needs about 52% a year growth, against 3% a year delivered over 3 years. So almost all of today's price rests on investors' willingness to pay a high multiple, not on current cash flow.
worth.key_assumption: The market keeps valuing Tesla within its own 5-year price-to-sales range rather than on its current 3.3B of free cash flow.

bull: Tesla holds 37.5B of net cash and 45.4B of liquidity, so it can fund heavy spending through a slow patch.
Twelve-month revenue still grew to 103.6B from 95.6B, and analysts expect 25% EPS growth next year.
R&D is 8.56% of revenue. The busiest call strike is 400 (open interest 26314), and the put/call open-interest ratio is a mild 0.76.
bear: Operating margin fell to 3.35% from 4.74%, and free cash flow halved to 3.3B from 6.8B.
Inventory is up 15% while quarterly sales are up 0%, which risks price cuts and thinner margins.
The stock trades at 412.0 times trailing earnings. Every DCF case is at or below 43.8, far below the 374.41 close.

levels.what: Today's close. It sits in the upper part of the own-history range and far above the DCF base of 24.48.
The top of the own-history price-to-sales range. Above it, even the most generous method calls the stock expensive.
The middle of the own-history range. Re-examine there only if operating margin rises back above 3.35% in the 2027-01-27 report.

longterm.why: Growth has stalled and margins and cash flow are shrinking, yet the price assumes a high multiple. The business is graded D and the committee call is Reduce.

swing.why: The trend is down, and price sits between support at 364.02–368.6 and resistance at 380.15–388.56. Both zones are close relative to the 16.14 average daily range, so a stop would sit inside normal noise. No trade until a close above 396.23 or below 364.02 shows a direction.

decision.timing: No new position before the 2027-01-27 report, the next real test of margins, inventory and cash flow. Options price a 3.7% move by 2026-11-20, 11.1% by 2026-12-18 and 19.0% by 2027-02-19, which spans earnings.

change_mind: The 2027-01-27 report shows operating margin back above 4.74% and quarterly sales growth back above 0% versus a year earlier.
Inventory growth falls back in line with sales growth, reversing the 15% versus 0% gap, while free cash flow recovers toward 6.8B.
Price drops to the 293.94 own-history midpoint while margins hold at or above 3.35%. That would reopen the long-term case.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still avoid. The 2.43% drop to 374.41 put the close below the 20-day, 50-day and 200-day averages while margins and cash flow kept shrinking.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
